harmfulness.reason: Following the core advice is unlikely to hurt the plant. "You only want to increase your pot size by one or two inches in diameter" is sound and guards against overpotting and root rot. Two minor issues: "Alternatively, you can line the bottom with a half-inch layer of grower's charcoal" implies charcoal can stand in for drainage holes in a non-draining pot, which is a questionable waterlogging risk. There is also no note that bird of paradise is mildly toxic to pets and children.

It ignores the poster's note that several plants share the pot, and includes store promotion ("Uni-Gro Premium Charcoal... in our retail store").
